question: Can the declared subpixel TX family and per-cell diagonal choice create terrain occlusion for the target's three full RX cells?
selected_experiment: C144 continuous convex-corridor clearance plus independent interval verification
excluded_in_declared_domain: Terrain occlusion from the declared source XY variation and height lower bound
Terrain occlusion from either diagonal or per-cell mixtures with the same candidate vertices
Ideal geometric direct-power attenuation through nonnegative convex interpolation within the three declared full RX cells
remaining_distinctions: Original numerical receiver stepping over untested source conditions
Release support outside the three declared RX cells
Different vertex coordinates/heights or source outside the declared domain
conditions: Terrain vertices equal the published Float32 candidate reconstruction.
Each ground grid cell may independently use either diagonal, with the same fixed Float32 vertices. Every triangle in both complete diagonal meshes was checked.
Each RX point is anywhere on either triangulation of one of the three full donor cells shifted +1m along z.
TX XY belongs to the stated rectangle, a hypothesis covering legacy coordinates and nearest/floor pixel-cell encodings under this candidate grid.
For LOS only, TX z may be any value at least zmin. For the inverse-square power bound TX z is restricted to [zmin,zmax].
The geometric LOS certificate does not guarantee numerical receiver-hit coverage or recover original scene coordinates.
